samples.text:
Nowadays more and more people decide to start their own business or work as freelancer instead of working for a company. In this essay I will explain the reasons for this choice and the qualities which a person need to be successful.

There are many reasons why people want to be self-employed. The biggest reason is freedom. When you work for yourself, you can decide your working hours and you do not have a boss who tells you what to do. For example, a graphic designer who is freelance can work from home and spend more time with his children. Another reason is money. In a company the salary is fixed, but if your own business is successful you can earn much more money. Also, some people are not happy with their job because they have a bad manager or boring tasks, so they decide to leave.

However, working for yourself is not easy and it needs some important qualities. First of all, a self-employed person must be very discipline. Nobody checks their work, so they must manage their time and meet deadlines without anybody help. Secondly, they need to be brave and take risk, because the income is not stable and in some months they can earn very little. Thirdly, good communication skills are important because they have to find customers and talk with them by themselves. Finally, they should be hard-working and ready to work long hours at the beginning.

In conclusion, people choose to work for themselves because they want freedom, more money and to escape from a bad job. To be successful, they need discipline, courage, communication skills and hard work.
samples.why: Both questions answered with relevant reasons and qualities · brief, general support · formulaic sequencing (First of all, Secondly) · repetitive vocabulary · errors in articles, word form and agreement that do not impede meaning.

samples.text:
An increasing number of people are leaving traditional employment to become freelancers, consultants or small business owners. This essay will outline the main motives behind this decision and discuss the personal qualities that are essential for success in self-employment.

The desire for independence is probably the most important motive. Employees often have little control over their schedules, the projects they work on or the way their performance is judged, whereas self-employed people can decide when, where and how they work. This flexibility is particularly attractive to parents with young children or people who want to combine work with travel. Financial ambition is another factor. While a salaried worker's income is usually limited by a fixed pay scale, a successful entrepreneur can benefit directly from their own effort and ideas. Some people also turn to self-employment out of frustration, for example after being overlooked for promotion or feeling that their skills are not valued.

Succeeding without an employer, however, demands a particular set of qualities. Self-discipline is the most crucial, since there is no manager to set deadlines or monitor progress, and it is easy to become distracted when working from home. Resilience is equally important, because income can be irregular and setbacks such as losing a major client are common, particularly in the first few years. In addition, independent workers need good interpersonal and marketing skills, as they are responsible for finding customers, negotiating prices and maintaining their reputation. Finally, they must be organised enough to handle practical matters such as taxes and invoices, which is often overlooked by people who is used to having an accounts department.

In conclusion, people choose self-employment mainly for independence, higher earning potential and escape from unsatisfying jobs. To succeed, they need self-discipline, resilience, strong communication skills and good organisation.
samples.why: Clear answers to both questions with extended, supported ideas · logical progression and good range of linkers · appropriate less common vocabulary (resilience, overlooked for promotion) · mostly error-free with two agreement slips.

samples.text:
For a growing share of the workforce, the security of a regular salary is no longer enough to outweigh the appeal of being one's own boss. People are drawn to self-employment for a mixture of personal and financial reasons, but turning that choice into a sustainable livelihood requires a demanding combination of character traits.

Autonomy lies at the heart of most decisions to go it alone. Working for an employer typically means accepting fixed hours, predetermined tasks and the judgement of a line manager, whereas independent workers can shape their own schedules and choose projects that genuinely interest them. For a parent who wants to be present at the school gate, or someone who does their best work late at night, this freedom can be transformative. There is also the prospect of greater reward: rather than seeing the benefits of their efforts absorbed by a company, the self-employed keep what they earn, and a thriving business may eventually generate far more than a salary ever would. Technology has made the leap less daunting, as online platforms allow even a single freelancer to reach clients around the world.

Yet freedom brings its own pressures, and certain qualities distinguish those who thrive from those who struggle. Self-motivation is paramount; without external deadlines or supervision, procrastination can quietly undermine a promising venture. Equally vital is resilience, since irregular income, demanding clients and unsuccessful pitches are an inevitable part of independent work. Successful freelancers also tend to be versatile, combining expertise in their field with the ability to market themselves, negotiate fees and manage finances. Finally, a degree of tolerance for risk is essential, as there is no guaranteed income at the end of each month.

In conclusion, people become self-employed chiefly to gain autonomy and to benefit directly from their own work. Achieving lasting success, however, depends on self-motivation, resilience, versatility and a willingness to live with uncertainty.
samples.why: Both parts thoroughly addressed with well-developed, illustrated ideas · cohesion managed naturally · wide, idiomatic vocabulary (go it alone, paramount, versatile) · wide range of accurate structures throughout.
